questions: Does slalom progress rise above 0.53, and do line_loss_events fall below 1.3 toward 1.0?
Does max_error on the slalom drop below 0.06 m, and does any slalom trial finish (report completion_time)?
Does s-bend steering_oscillation stay under 0.35, and does the s-bend hold 20/20 as in iteration 7?
On the slalom, what heading is the robot at when it first loses the line? Is the failure overshoot at direction changes or line loss at entry?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If the slalom line loss rises or the s-bend oscillation exceeds 0.35, return to mass 0.6 kg with wheel_track 0.10 m (the iteration 7 design). If the slalom progress rises but line loss stays at about 1.3 or higher, report the entry heading and speed so the controller entry speed can be the next lever instead of more geometry.

intent: Revert wheel_track to 0.10 m, which scored best (iteration 7, 707.2), and reduce mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg to lower yaw inertia about 17 percent further, testing whether a faster-turning robot keeps the slalom line for longer. Sensing and the rest of the body are unchanged. The Integrator should keep kp and kd from iteration 7 so the race isolates the mass change. If the score falls below 707 or s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds 0.35, return to mass 0.6 kg with wheel_track 0.10 m.
learning: Narrowing wheel_track to 0.09 m (iteration 8) raised s-bend jitter to 0.342 and cut slalom progress from 0.53 to 0.42, so turn authority has an upper limit that the slalom does not benefit from. Lower yaw inertia remains the only geometry lever that moved slalom progress. Mass 0.5 kg tests whether that lever continues or starts to overshoot.
rationale: Iteration 8 narrowed wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m and scored 683.7, below the iteration 7 best of 707.2. The oval held 20/20 at 1.76 s, so the track change did not break the oval. The s-bend lost a finish (19/20, one off-track at min 391.8) and its steering_oscillation rose from 0.311 to 0.342, close to the 0.35 limit. The slalom improved only slightly: line_loss_events fell from 1.3 to 1.2, but mean progress fell from 0.53 to 0.42 and max_error stayed at 0.0655, past the 0.06 limit. More turn authority from the narrower track therefore added s-bend jitter and cost slalom progress without fixing the slalom exit. The next step is to return wheel_track to 0.10 m, the best-measured value. The slalom still needs a change that it has not yet received. Lower yaw inertia (iteration 7) was the only change that moved slalom progress (0.30 to 0.53). I therefore test one more step in that direction: mass 0.5 kg with body_length 0.12 m, about 17 percent lower yaw inertia (0.5*(0.0144+0.0144)/12 = 0.0012 kg·m² against 0.00144). Sensing (7 sensors at 0.012 m pitch, span ±0.036 m, 12 mm footprints, lead 0.06 m), wheel_radius 0.03 m and body_width 0.12 m stay as in iteration 7. Expected result: slalom progress keeps rising above 0.53 and line_loss_events move toward 1.0, while the oval stays 20/20 and the s-bend stays at or above 19/20 with steering_oscillation under 0.35. Risk: a lighter, faster-turning robot may overshoot at direction changes, as iteration 7 already hinted (line loss rose to 1.3). If that happens or the s-bend oscillation exceeds 0.35, the fallback is the iteration 7 design (mass 0.6 kg, track 0.10 m).
